question: What nomenclatural candidates does the current Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes provide for the nine fish-name labels in Parañaque EIS Table 2.2-19, and can those names be normalized or treated as verified fish records?

method.authority: California Academy of Sciences, Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes
method.authorityVersion: Selected Catalog pages displayed updates in August or September 2026. Indexed record excerpts and bounded name queries were checked on 2026-11-24; attempts to open the individual Catalog pages returned HTTP 403 in the web reader.
queries: Valamugil cunnesius and current accepted usage
method.sourceTable: Official final EIS Table 2.2-19, printed report pages 2.2-95 to 2.2-96. Nine fish-name rows were transcribed from the already reviewed parent assessment; the blue swimmer crab row was excluded from the fish-name cross-check.
method.interpretation: Catalog status informs nomenclature only. It does not identify the EIS organisms, establish a Parañaque or Manila Bay occurrence, verify the English/local-name pairings, or resolve a catch event, date, survey activity, station, or coordinate. Candidate spellings are not automatic corrections.

sourceCitation: City Government of Parañaque (2021), Environmental Impact Statement Report: Proposed 286.86 Hectare Parañaque Reclamation Project, Table 2.2-19; Fricke, R., Eschmeyer, W. N. & Van der Laan, R. (eds.), Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, California Academy of Sciences, selected records checked 2026-11-24.

fishNameCrosswalk.catalogStatus: Current status: valid as Oreochromis niloticus.
fishNameCrosswalk.decision: Record niloticus as a nomenclatural spelling candidate only. Preserve the EIS string and do not infer that its reported fish was identified as this species.

fishNameCrosswalk.catalogStatus: Current status: valid as Mugil cephalus.
fishNameCrosswalk.decision: Record cephalus as a spelling candidate only. Keep the source spelling and hold specimen identity and vernacular pairing.

fishNameCrosswalk.catalogStatus: The Catalog lists Valamugil cunnesius as a published valid usage and currently gives Moolgarda cunnesius as valid.
fishNameCrosswalk.decision: The EIS spelling is a candidate variant of cunnesius, and Moolgarda is the Catalog's current usage. This is not an identification of the EIS fish; preserve the printed string.

fishNameCrosswalk.catalogStatus: Current status: valid as Clupanodon thrissa.
fishNameCrosswalk.decision: Nomenclatural usage agrees with the source label. No specimen identity or location-resolved occurrence is asserted.

fishNameCrosswalk.catalogStatus: Current status: valid as Gerres filamentosus.
fishNameCrosswalk.decision: Nomenclatural usage agrees with the source label. No specimen identity or location-resolved occurrence is asserted.

fishNameCrosswalk.catalogStatus: The Catalog lists species in genus Siganus; the EIS label itself does not identify a species.
fishNameCrosswalk.decision: Retain as an unresolved genus-level label. Do not choose a species or convert it to a species-level record.

fishNameCrosswalk.catalogStatus: Current status: valid as Rastrelliger kanagurta.
fishNameCrosswalk.decision: Nomenclatural usage agrees with the source label. No specimen identity or location-resolved occurrence is asserted.

fishNameCrosswalk.catalogStatus: The source label is a family-level identification, not a binomial species name.
fishNameCrosswalk.decision: Keep at family rank. Do not infer an anchovy species from the English or local name.

fishNameCrosswalk.rankAsPrinted: genus-level placeholder with unresolved source genus spelling
fishNameCrosswalk.catalogStatus: The Catalog includes the genus Leiognathus; this does not establish that the EIS's printed Leiognatus was intended to mean Leiognathus.
fishNameCrosswalk.decision: Preserve Leiognatus sp verbatim and hold the genus spelling and species identity for expert/source review. No species-level crosswalk is made.

excludedNonFishRows.reason: The EIS labels this row as blue swimmer crab; it is outside the fish-name cross-check.

limitations: The Catalog's nomenclatural status does not authenticate any organism or field identification in the EIS.
The EIS does not connect individual table labels or catch-rate summaries to a particular date, fishing event, survey activity, station, coordinate, specimen, or voucher.
Two labels remain above species rank, and Leiognatus sp is not safely resolvable from the printed string alone.
No item-specific permission to redistribute the EIS table or its derived fish list was identified in the parent review.
The Catalog pages were evaluated from indexed record extracts because individual page opens returned HTTP 403; the bounded check is not a complete taxonomic review.
decision: Keep all nine EIS fish names as source-verbatim, research-only labels with the bounded Catalog nomenclature notes above. Do not normalize the EIS table, assert a species identity, assign any label to a catch event or station, add occurrence or app rows, or reproduce the table. The crab row is excluded from fish taxa. NCR and Luzon remain incomplete.
followUps: Obtain an expert review or independently accessible source copy before changing any EIS scientific-name spelling or source-to-species mapping.
Find locality- and event-resolved Parañaque or Manila Bay evidence and review its own methods, vouchers, and rights before considering any occurrence record.
Request item-specific reuse terms before redistributing EIS-derived names or table content.
